exam_scheme.note: The Foreign Medical Graduate Examination (FMGE) is a statutory screening test conducted twice a year (June and December cycles) by the National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) under the Screening Test Regulations, 2002 of the National Medical Commission (NMC). An Indian citizen or OCI cardholder possessing a primary medical qualification awarded by any medical institution outside India must qualify FMGE to obtain provisional or permanent registration with the NMC or any State Medical Council. The test is delivered via Computer Based Test (CBT) and comprises 300 multiple-choice questions carrying 300 marks, divided into two equal parts: Part A (150 questions, 150 minutes) covering Pre- and Para-Clinical subjects, and Part B (150 questions, 150 minutes) covering Clinical subjects. There is NO negative marking. To qualify, a candidate must obtain a minimum of 150 marks out of 300 (50%).
